Package br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.infrastructure.persistence

Class PostgresGymRepository

java.lang.Object
br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.infrastructure.persistence.PostgresGymRepository
All Implemented Interfaces:
GymRepository
public final class PostgresGymRepository extends Object implements GymRepository
Keeps the gym's structure in three PostgreSQL tables — the gym, its courts with their labels, and their cameras — reached through plain JDBC.

The tables are private to this class, and the class creates them when they are missing. Saving replaces the whole gym inside one transaction, so the database never holds half of one. Loading rebuilds the gym only through the domain's own behaviour, so rows edited by hand cannot produce a gym the domain would have refused. Values reach SQL only as bound parameters.

  • Method Details

    • open

      public static PostgresGymRepository open(String url, String user, String password) throws RepositoryException
      Connects to the database and creates the gym's tables when they are missing. Tables that already exist are left as they are, the stored gym included.
      Parameters:
      url - the JDBC url of the PostgreSQL database
      user - the database user
      password - the user's password, which may be empty for a local database
      Returns:
      a repository whose tables are ready
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the url or the user is missing
      RepositoryException - if the database cannot be reached or the tables cannot be created

    • save

      public void save(Gym gym) throws RepositoryException
      Stores the gym as it is now, replacing whatever was stored before.

      If any statement fails, the transaction is rolled back and the gym stored before stays exactly as it was.

      Specified by:
      save in interface GymRepository
      Parameters:
      gym - the gym to keep
      Throws:
      RepositoryException - if the storage cannot be written

    • load

      public Optional<Gym> load() throws RepositoryException
      Reads back the gym stored last.

      The three tables are read in one snapshot, so a save committed halfway through a load cannot mix two gyms.

      Specified by:
      load in interface GymRepository
      Returns:
      the stored gym, or empty when nothing has been stored yet
      Throws:
      RepositoryException - if what is stored cannot be read back as a gym
